messages:
maria (support): FYI from a paying customer — multiple 502s and auth timeouts hitting hosted inference this morning, starting ~10:02 UTC. They say token verification errors and also spikes in latency. Escalating to war room. @emily can you pick this up?

emily (oncall): I'm on it. can anyone confirm whether this is isolated to their org or widespread?

support-bot: New escalation created: Ticket #INC-4872 — customer reported 502 and 401_timed_out. Added :rotating_light:

aj (sre): I see a jump in 5xx rate at 10:01:45 across the hosted gateway cluster in eu-west-1. Error mix: 502 gateway, 504 upstream, and some 401-token-verify-timeout. Rolling 1m avg 5xx from 0.1% -> 3.2%.

patrick (eng-runtime): Logs show a lot of upstream service "auth-verifier" returning 503 with "deadline exceeded" around same window. Could be overload or a config change. Any recent deploys?

lee (infra): No infra deploys at that time. There was an autoscaler activity on the gateway ASG at 09:59 due to memory pressure, nodes evicted and rejoined. Noting: session-affinity was temporarily disabled during the scale event (we're investigating why the toggle flipped).

emily (oncall): Repro steps from support: curl to our hosted endpoint => some requests immediately 502, some return 401 with body: "token verification timed out". Provided sample request id abc123. Can we tail logs for that request id?

patrick (eng-runtime): Tailing request abc123: stack: gateway -> auth-verifier -> token-cache -> runtime. auth-verifier logs: "rpc call to token-service timed out (deadline exceeded)". token-service shows elevated tail-latency and >50% connection retries.

aj (sre): Overlaying traces — many in-flight requests were being routed to different runtime pods after the ASG churn. We rely on session-affinity to keep KV cache hit rates high for auth tokens. If affinity broke, token-cache miss rates spike and token-service gets hammered. That matches symptoms.

maria (support): Customer notes that the errors ended around 10:20 and they got partial success on retries but want credits and root cause. They're also worried about auth failures that looked like "invalid token" at times.

lee (infra): Confirmed: autoscaler triggered due to a memory leak in one older gateway node; ASG replaced the node. During replacement, an ingress controller rolling update (kube-proxy restart) inadvertently set session-affinity mode to "None" for a short window due to a bad annotation rollout script. Ops change: the affinity toggle is stored in a configmap that had an ownerRef replaced.

patrick (eng-runtime): Runtime also got a small config bump 09:58 that adjusted keepalive timeout for token-service RPCs from 5s -> 3s (attempt to reduce resource spikes). Combination of affinity loss + reduced keepalive = token-service saw more concurrent cold calls and tighter deadlines -> timeouts and 503s.

aj (sre): Mitigation applied 10:06:00 — revert runtime keepalive to 5s and re-enable session-affinity at the ingress level (force sync). Within 2–3 minutes 5xx rate dropped back to baseline. We also put a temporary rate limiter on unauthenticated token revalidations.

emily (oncall): Customer notified at 10:25 with summary and we're offering a credit. Logged internal incident and created initial marker for postmortem.

maria (support): Customer asked for repro steps — we documented and provided sample request id + suggestion to retry with exponential backoff. Noted that retrying within 30s helped for many of their requests.

sre-bot: Deployed mitigation rollback: runtime-keepalive reverted (deploy id: d-2026-09-14-1006). Circuit breaker added to auth-verifier: 1000r/s threshold.

patrick (eng-runtime): Postmortem TODOs brainstorm: 1) fix configmap ownerRef issue that allowed affinity toggle to flip during rolling updates; 2) add a safety check to prevent affinity annotation removal during node replacement; 3) increase token-service headroom + circuit breakers; 4) add alert that correlates configmap changes with 5xx spikes.

lee (infra): I'll own #1 and #2. Proposed action: lock the configmap via admission controller and add a Canary rollout guard so the affinity annotation can't be removed without explicit approval.

aj (sre): I'll own #3 and #4. Also propose adding a temporary golden route — route critical customers to a pre-warmed token-cache pool during scaling events. Need product/rt-check.

maria (support): Action: send follow-up email to customer with RCA ETA and offer credit. I'll own comms.

emily (oncall): Quick short-term actions completed: rolled back keepalive, forced ingress affinity on all active nodes, applied rate limiter to token-verifications. Medium-term items scheduled.

patrick (eng-runtime): CAPTURED NOTES for postmortem: root cause = race of (autoscaler-caused node churn) + (ingress config mutation removing session-affinity) + (aggressive RPC keepalive reducing timeouts) -> cold token-cache storm -> token-service RPC timeouts -> 502/504/401_timed_out observed by customers.

maria (support): Customer wants to see the PM postmortem and updated SLOs around auth verification. I'll coordinate.

aj (sre): Immediate remediation tickets: INC-4872-01 lock-configmap, INC-4872-02 add-affinity-guard, INC-4872-03 token-service-headroom, INC-4872-04 alert-configmap-change. Assigning owners and due dates in ops board.

lee (infra): ETA for configmap admission controller PR: 3 days. Canary guard: 5 days.

patrick (eng-runtime): Runtime fix to revert keepalive permanent? I'll propose a safer change: adaptive keepalive plus client-side retry with jitter. PR planned in 4 days.

emily (oncall): Any outstanding asks? If not I'll close the war room in 1 hour and move to postmortem channel.

maria (support): No more asks from the customer now. Thanks everyone. Please add any follow-ups to the incident board. :thumbsup:
